chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear al-Khazz in the winter, and the al-Khazz shawl, and a hood of al-Khazz. He would spend the winter in it, and sell the shawl in the summer and give charity with its price.
Then he would say: [Quran 7:32] "Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions?"

key_terms.الخَزّ: Al-Khazz: a fabric woven from a mixture of silk and wool or other fibers, considered permissible to wear unlike pure silk which is forbidden for men
key_terms.القَلَنْسُوَة: Al-Qalansuwa: a type of hood or head covering
key_terms.المِطْرَف: Al-Mitraf: a large embroidered shawl or cloak worn over the shoulders
key_terms.زِينَةَ اللَّهِ: Adornments of God: the beautiful and permissible things God has created for human use

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Zayn al-Abidin wear al-Khazz fabric and what is its ruling in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) narrates from Abu al-Hasan al-Washa' that Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), would wear garments of al-Khazz — a permissible silk-mixed fabric — in winter, sell the shawl in summer, and donate the proceeds to charity. This practice was accompanied by his recitation of Quran 7:32, using the Quranic verse as a jurisprudential proof that wearing fine clothing is not prohibited, since God has made such adornments permissible for His servants. The narration reflects the Imami position that piety does not require abstinence from lawful enjoyment of worldly blessings.
